page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.m1.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the ecs.m1 server family. It is built on the KVM hypervisor and utilizes the x86_64 CPU architecture. The instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB of memory allocated per core.

This instance configuration does not include local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met through external block storage volumes. Additionally, the ecs.m1.xlarge does not feature any GPU hardware accelerators, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

An analysis of the CPU flags reveals that this instance lacks support for advanced instruction sets. Specifically, there is no hardware-level availability for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512), Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), or cryptographic acceleration features such as AES-NI and SHA-NI. It also lacks virtualization extensions (VMX/SVM) and hyper-threading (HT) flags. These omissions limit its efficiency for specialized vector math, machine learning inference, and hardware-accelerated encryption.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation and standard memory-to-core ratio, the ecs.m1.xlarge offers a predictable resource profile for standard workloads. It is designed for general-purpose applications, basic web serving, and lightweight database hosting that do not require high-performance vector processing or local NVMe storage.
